name: Note
text: Drop plates, stock footage, or phone test shots here. Start simple — a static tripod shot of a room or object is enough to learn tracking and compositing on.

name: Note
text: Links to the tutorials/courses you are following right now. Note which software each one uses (Nuke, After Effects, Blender, Fusion, DaVinci Resolve) so you don't mix workflows mid-lesson.

name: Note
text:
1. Green/blue screen keying
2. Simple rotoscoping (mask an object)
3. Color match two clips
4. Add a basic particle effect (dust, smoke)
5. Track a static object onto footage
6. Export a final render at correct resolution/fps

name: Note
text: Which tool are you using and why? (e.g. DaVinci Resolve Fusion — free, node-based, good first compositor. Blender — free, also does 3D if you want to add CG elements later.)

name: Note
text: Mismatched black levels/gamma between plate and CG. Motion blur missing on fast-moving comped elements. Keying edges too hard (no edge feather). Forgetting to match grain/noise between elements.

name: Note
text: A "levitating object" shot (wire removal + subtle motion). A day-to-night sky replacement. A simple muzzle-flash / laser-beam effect added to a phone video.
